## 1. Intro and scope

- Fun question: careful data modeling plus **fan-out**, a concept that recurs across SD problems
- Scope: a now-dated Facebook variant
  - Users follow each other **unidirectionally**
  - **Chronological** feed
  - Modern feeds lean on ML ranking; out of scope (see their video-recommendation breakdown for MLEs)

## 2. Delivery framework

- Tens of thousands of mocks: candidates with a system make more progress, get stuck less
1. Requirements: constraints, uncertainties, the crux
2. Core entities: nouns; drive data model and API
3. API: stubs; a design that implements them is "halfway done"
4. Data flow: data-processing problems only (not here)
5. HLD: meet functional requirements simply, warts noted
6. Deep dives: bottlenecks, lingering NFRs, the interviewer's lead
- Goal: a working system on the whiteboard in ~35 minutes

## 3. Requirements

- Functional
  - **Create posts**
  - **Follow users**
  - **View the feed**
  - **Page through the feed** (users scroll: a page, then more)
- Tip: imagine the open app: what's shown, what can you do?
- Likes, comments, privacy settings: keep it simple; beyond 3–4 items, mark extras as below the line/bonus
  - Out of time? Skip listing below-the-line items and move on
- Don't rush requirements, but spend only a few minutes
- Non-functional
  - **Eventual consistency**: posts needn't appear instantly, but quickly; **≤ 1 minute** to appear in feeds
  - **Latency: 500 ms** for posting and viewing (users get annoyed after a few hundred ms)
  - **Scale: ~2B users** ("we don't need to know exactly")

## 4. Core entities

- **User**, **Post**, **Follow** (relationship)
- News feed = find posts from users you follow
- No attributes yet; add them during the HLD

## 5. API

```
POST /posts                    body: { content }       -> 201 { postId }
PUT  /users/:id/followers      (no body)
GET  /feed?pageSize=25&cursor  -> { posts[], nextCursor }
```

- APIs needn't be 1:1 with requirements, but must cover them
- HLD is done when it implements every API
- Unfollow: no requirement, but a sensible extension interviewers ask about
- **Cursor = a timestamp**: how deep into the feed the user has gone
  - Next request returns N items older than it; nothing is missed as the user scrolls
- REST or not? gRPC works if you control clients, even function signatures
  - Learn REST: it's standard, and avoids yellow flags from "REST zealot interviewers"

## 6. HLD: create posts

- Build the most basic working system first; candidates lose themselves in micro-optimizations
- **Post service** behind an **API gateway + load balancer**
- **DynamoDB** (or Cassandra, any scalable wide-column store)
- Post: creator, content, createdAt
- Scales by adding post services, "provided we don't blow up DynamoDB"

## 7. HLD: follow users

- No graph DB needed
  - Graph DBs (Neo4j, Cypher) help with comprehensions like "users followed by at least two people who follow each other"
  - We only need "who follows X" and "whom does X follow"
- Start with simple, tightly fit approaches; complexity early ties you in knots
  - Simplicity is "a hallmark differentiator" of senior vs junior candidates
- **Follow service** writes a **Follow table**
  - Partition key = userFollowing, sort key = userFollowed: list whom A follows
  - **GSI** reversed (partition = userFollowed, sort = userFollowing): list A's followers
    - GSI ≈ another table maintained consistently by DynamoDB (Cassandra: secondary index)
- DynamoDB range queries return ≤ **1 MB** per request, then page
  - ~10 bytes per entry → a bit under 100K entries per request
  - A problem for the most-followed accounts only

## 8. HLD: view and page the feed

- New **feed service**: read-heavy, bears most traffic; feed generation can be compute-heavy
- Reads the post and follow tables directly
  - A microservice purist wants APIs in front of those tables; here the overhead dwarfs the benefit
  - If your interviewer is a stickler, do it
- Flow
  1. Query follows for the user
  2. Query each followed user's recent posts
  3. Merge and return
- Need: posts by creator → **GSI on posts**: creatorId, sorted by createdAt
- Alarm bells: following many users; creators with many posts
  - Acknowledge verbally; commit to deep dives; keep traction on functional requirements
- Pagination: for each followed user, fetch ≤ pageSize posts with createdAt < cursor
- Works for many users, not for those following or followed by many

## 9. Deep dive: users following many accounts (precomputed feed)

- Following 10,000 accounts: 10,000 GSI queries, ~10M posts to merge and sort near real time
  - Plus failures and tail latency
- Instinct: compute at write time, not read time
- **Precomputed feed table** (in DynamoDB for simplicity; could be a cache)
  - On post: read followers from the follow GSI; append the post ID to each follower's feed
  - Feed service reads the precomputed feed directly: "super fast"
- Keep it bounded: latest **200 post IDs** per user
  - 10 B per ID × 200 = **2 KB/user**
  - Gut check: Facebook earns ~$100 per US user per year; 2 KB is nothing
  - 2B users × 2 KB = **2 TB**: reasonable
- Write-up frames this deep dive as "users following many users" (write-up)

## 10. Deep dive: accounts with many followers (async, hybrid)

- New problem: an account with 10,000+ followers posts → tens of thousands of feed writes
  - "A thunderstorm of activity"
- Not synchronous in the post service (the Hello Interview page shouldn't wait 60 s to post)
- **Async worker pool**
  - Post created → entry on a queue
  - Feed workers read followers from the GSI
  - Big lists split into sub-jobs back on the queue, spreading load
  - Workers write the post ID into each follower's precomputed feed
- Mega accounts (Justin Bieber, hundreds of millions of followers): broadcasting probably not appropriate
  - Plus the DynamoDB 1 MB paging limits on follower lists
- **Hybrid feeds**
  - Add a flag on each follow: **precomputed or not**
  - Not precomputed when the followed account is huge (e.g., 100K+ followers)
  - Workers write to feeds only for precomputed follows
  - Feed service at read time: precomputed feed + latest posts from non-precomputed follows, merged
  - Caps writes per post and reads per feed
- The rabbit hole continues (good follow-ups)
  - Following many huge accounts? Unfollows? Does the flag ever reverse?
- Product limits beat engineering to infinity
  - Google won't show page 1,000; LinkedIn caps connections
  - Not worth engineering around the 0.0001% of users
- Write-up labels: blast the requests (bad); async workers (good); async workers with hybrid feeds (great) (write-up)

## 11. Deep dive: hot posts (hot key)

- A viral post tops millions of feeds; everyone fetches the same post ID
- **Hot key / hot shard**
  - DynamoDB scales only within its assumptions: roughly even load across keys
  - Partitions are physical hosts with real limits; all traffic to host A gets throttled
- **Post cache** (LFU eviction + TTL)
  - Posts rarely change; small memory needed (only hottest posts)
  - Common mid/senior answer, but a cache sharded by post ID **has the same hot key**
  - Redis may absorb it in memory, but the problem remains
- **Redundant cache instances**
  - Multiple independent cache instances, not shards; feed service picks one at random
  - No replication or coordination needed
  - DynamoDB sees at most N requests (N instances), not millions
- Write-up labels: post cache with large keyspace (good); redundant post cache (great) (write-up)
- Interviewers often take over here to probe weak points, even ones you flagged
  - Not a sign you're wrong; they drive to the depth they need
  - Much of the signal is implicit: your process, not just the whiteboard

## 12. Wrap-up and levels

- Pattern for deep dives: find a bottleneck, propose solutions, find their bottlenecks, repeat
- Concepts: async worker pools, fan-out, hot keys, sharding
- Write-up bars (write-up)
  - E4: clear API and data model; working HLD; some "good" solutions; not every edge case
  - E5: speed through HLD; 2+ deep dives in detail; proactively surface fan-out and performance issues
  - Staff: likely all deep dives (or others); surface issues; performance tuning

## 13. Board as text (assembled from the talk)

```
Client -> API GW / LB -> Post Service -> Posts (DynamoDB; GSI creator+createdAt)
                      |                    \-> Queue -> Feed workers (fan-out,
                      |                                 split big jobs)
                      -> Follow Service -> Follow (PK following, SK followed;
                      |                    GSI reversed; precomputed flag)
                      -> Feed Service  -> Precomputed feed (200 IDs/user)
                                       + live merge for huge accounts
                                       -> redundant post caches (random pick)
```
